scenes.heading: Table inheritance
scenes.caption: Inheritance lets a new class start from an existing class and then add or replace behaviour. The new class is the child. The existing one is the parent. It is useful when several types really are the same kind of thing with a twist. It is harmful when you use it only to reuse a few lines.

items: Inheritance lets a new class start from an existing class and then add or replace behaviour
The new class is the child
The existing one is the parent
It is useful when several types really are the same kind of thing with a twist. It is harmful when you use it only to reuse a few lines

scenes.heading: Step by step: Table inheritance
scenes.caption: Name what is truly shared. That belongs on the parent. Put only the difference on the child. Call the parent's setup so the child is fully initialised. If the “is a kind of” sentence sounds fake, do not inherit. Compose instead.

items: Name what is truly shared. That belongs on the parent.

scenes.caption: Here is a small example of Table inheritance. Read each line and say what it changes. class Animal: has a name class Dog(Animal): adds bark() A Dog is an Animal. A Car with a name is not an Animal, even if copying the field would be easy. If you can change one piece and predict the new result, you have it.

scenes.heading: role inheritance
scenes.caption: Inheritance lets a new class start from an existing class and then add or replace behaviour. The new class is the child. The existing one is the parent. It is useful when several types really are the same kind of thing with a twist. It is harmful when you use it only to reuse a few lines.

items: Inheritance lets a new class start from an existing class and then add or replace behaviour
The new class is the child
The existing one is the parent
It is useful when several types really are the same kind of thing with a twist. It is harmful when you use it only to reuse a few lines

scenes.heading: Step by step: role inheritance
scenes.caption: Name what is truly shared. That belongs on the parent. Put only the difference on the child. Call the parent's setup so the child is fully initialised. If the “is a kind of” sentence sounds fake, do not inherit. Compose instead.

items: Name what is truly shared. That belongs on the parent.

scenes.heading: Example: role inheritance
scenes.caption: Here is a small example of role inheritance. Read each line and say what it changes. class Animal: has a name class Dog(Animal): adds bark() A Dog is an Animal. A Car with a name is not an Animal, even if copying the field would be easy. If you can change one piece and predict the new result, you have it.

scenes.heading: Variables
scenes.caption: Variables are names for values. Each name is a label, and the value is whatever is stored under that label at this moment. Almost every program you write is a set of named values being changed on purpose. If the names are clear, the program is explainable.

scenes.heading: Step by step: Variables
scenes.caption: Give each value a name that says what it is for. Read a name to get the current value. Assign a new value when the fact changes. Keep one meaning per name. Do not reuse score for a user's email.

scenes.heading: encryption
scenes.caption: Encryption turns readable data into unreadable data using a key. Decryption turns it back, and only with the right key. It protects data from being read. It does not, by itself, prove who sent it. That is a signature.

scenes.heading: Step by step: encryption
scenes.caption: Choose what must be unreadable: the password store, the disk, the connection. Use a standard algorithm already in your platform. Do not invent one. Protect the key. Encrypted data with a key in the same folder is not protected. Passwords are hashed, not encrypted, so you cannot decrypt them and you should not want to.

scenes.heading: HTML
scenes.caption: HTML is the language that describes the structure of a web page: headings, paragraphs, links, images, forms. The browser turns those tags into a document people can use. CSS and JavaScript sit on top of this structure. If the HTML is wrong, the page can look fine and still be unusable by a keyboard or a screen reader.

items: HTML is the language that describes the structure of a web page: headings, paragraphs, links, images, forms
The browser turns those tags into a document people can use
CSS and JavaScript sit on top of this structure. If the HTML is wrong, the page can look fine and still be unusable by a keyboard or a screen reader
